newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes slip on outright price pressures.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes slip on outright price pressures.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices retreated Thursday morning on outright technical and fundamental pressures, while domestic barrels steadied.
July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing benchmark prices were pegged at $19.90-$20.00, some 15 cents firmer than NYMEX futures, but 35 cents weaker than late Wednesday measurements.
Cash continued to hold sway over the NYMEX screen due to firm July Exchange for Physicals (EFPs) rates. Traders said the latest talk put EFPs at plus 13-16 cents, against last trades at +15 cents.
July WTI cash was steady to around five cents weaker than August NYMEX screen values.

Refiners worried about foreign barrels being delivered against NYMEX contracts have propped the EFP market in recent weeks. Foreign deliveries against the May and June NYMEX contracts were expected to occur in July as well, though just the threat of more foreign deliveries bolstered EFPs.

NYMEX markets deflated on liquidation by speculative players, and continued worries over bearish inventory stock data, which showed extremely high refinery run rates and builds for crude and products.
On the grade front, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James refused to budge from a 16-13 cents discount to marker WTI, with last recorded deals heard late Wednesday at -17 cents.
Weaker numbers for Dated Brent and a lack of demand for bringing North Sea Brent barrels to the U.S. Gulf played into market psychology.

Sour grades had a softer tone, partially due to weaker Far East prices. Iraqi oil will also remain in the market, following Wednesday's renewal of the oil-for-food accord. Traders expected the U.N. to maintain the oil deal, so there was no price shock, just the realization Iraqi exports will continue, keeping 700,000 barrels per day of crude in play.
West Texas Sour/Midland was talked at a $1.65-55 discount, with Eugene Island falling back to a $1.75-70 under WTI.
